A.explanation: A is at the equilibrium $y=0$ at the same $x$ as X. X starts at a crest and reaches equilibrium after a quarter period, not after $t=1\text{ s}$.

B.explanation: B is at the same $x$ as X but with opposite displacement. After half an oscillation the crest particle is at the trough.

C.explanation: C is at a different $x$ from X. In a transverse wave the rope particle does not travel forward with the wave, so its $x$ cannot change.

D.explanation: D is a crest one wavelength ahead of X. The wave shape moves to the right but the marked piece of rope X stays at its original $x$.

hints: Notice which labelled points share the same $x$-coordinate as X. In a transverse rope wave, the particle moves only in $y$ and keeps the same $x$.
Use the given frequency $0.5\text{ Hz}$ to find the period $T=1/f$. Compare the elapsed time $t=1\text{ s}$ with $T$.
X starts at maximum positive $y$ at $t=0$. Think what the displacement of a particle in simple harmonic motion is after exactly half a period.
walkthrough: At $t=0$ the graph of $y$ against $x$ shows X at a crest, with maximum positive displacement. Points A and B have the same $x$ as X, so only A or B can be the later position of the same piece of rope.

For a transverse wave the particles oscillate perpendicular to propagation. The wave moves in $+x$ but X does not move in $x$, it only moves up and down in $y$. This rules out C and D at different $x$ values.
The particle oscillation frequency is $0.5\text{ Hz}$, so the period is $T = 1/f = 1/0.5 = 2.0\text{ s}$.
The time elapsed is $t = 1\text{ s} = T/2$, exactly half an oscillation. A particle starting at a crest is at equilibrium after $T/4$ and at the opposite extreme, the trough, after $T/2$.
Therefore X moves from maximum $+y$ to maximum $-y$ at the same $x$. This is option B.
